intro: Iceland's economy runs on fish, aluminium, tourism and almost entirely renewable energy.

chapters.title: Fish and clean power
text: Fishing has always been the backbone of the economy. Almost all of Iceland's electricity comes from hydropower and geothermal energy, and most homes are heated with water from hot springs; that cheap power attracts aluminium smelters and data centres.

chapters.title: Tourism and the crash
text: Tourism boomed after 2010, with millions of visitors a year. In 2008 the collapse of Iceland's banks caused a deep recession, but the economy recovered. Iceland uses its own currency, the króna.

keyTerms.meaning: Heat and power from hot water and steam underground.
